content.text: May I suggest fcrepo-dto-foxml for this?
It's in central, and it can be used to easily, programmatically construct Fedora objects and serialize them to FOXML.
Documentation, including javadocs, can be found here:
http://cwilper.github.com/fcrepo-misc/fcrepo-dto/index.html
For an example project that uses this library, see
https://github.com/cwilper/fcrepo-dto-example

Im not sure what T1 and T2 stand for in "... where 10% are of type T1, 50% type T2". Are these mimetypes of the datastreams like images and pdfs, or are T1 and T2 meant to stand for FOXML1.1, METS, etc..?
uploaded a first simple version of a random object geenrator:
https://github.com/fasseg/fedora-objects-factory
split up the factories for datastreams, fedora objects and FOXMLs, and added support for different controlgroups.
see
https://github.com/fasseg/fedora-objects-factory
I'm not sure about how to generate the user interface. I thought the best approach would be a command line interface like the fcrepo-installer offers so it can be easily used via SSH.
Is this ok or did you guys imagine a GUI in order to be able to click a test set together?
the current approach is here:
https://github.com/fasseg/fedora-objects-factory/blob/master/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/dto/factories/cli/CommandlineGenerator.java
I wasn't imagining a GUI
So were you rather thinking about controlling the generator via a properties file or command line switches?
added a property handling interactive command line interface for the end-user.
you can check it out by building
https://github.com/fasseg/fedora-objects-factory/
and running java -jar target/fedora-objects-generator-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar

I should be able to build a suite of Fedora test objects according to configuration parameters which include composition of datastreams (e.g. X, M, E, R), relations to other objects, along with distribution of said objects that are also configurable (e.g. 100,000 objects, where 10% are of type T1, 50% type T2, etc).
In the case of M datastreams, we should be able to specify inlined base64 or not.
